subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub explicitly govern instructions addressed to the agent, and should declared capabilities reduce scrutiny without making otherwise out-of-scope or consent-bypassing instructions acceptable?
rationale: Current policy is adjacent but does not settle the normative boundary for model-directed prose or borderline declared behavior; automation cannot safely choose that security and moderation policy.

options.title: Add explicit agent-instruction policy
options.body: Allow task-scoped usage instructions, prohibit privilege escalation and consent bypass, and make declared external behavior reviewable rather than automatically allowed.

options.title: Rely on general policy
options.body: Treat existing unsafe-execution, misleading-requirement, and confirmation-boundary language as sufficient without a separate agent-directed category.

options.title: Consolidate under the broader RFC
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2321 the sole policy venue after preserving this issue's agent-specific examples and open questions there.

recommendation.title: Add explicit agent-instruction policy
recommendation.body: Allow task-scoped usage instructions, prohibit privilege escalation and consent bypass, and make declared external behavior reviewable rather than automatically allowed.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository contributor guidance assigns this handle the clearest ClawHub and community moderation ownership signal.
